stem: A DLI calculation is based on one PPFD reading taken at the brightest canopy location. What is the strongest reason to question using that value as the room-wide daily light dose?
choices: The brightest-point PPFD may not represent the spatial photon distribution experienced across the canopy during the photoperiod
The calculation may still be representative if the photoperiod is measured accurately, because DLI mathematically integrates time with the selected PPFD value
A bright-point reading is appropriate when fixture output is stable, since spatial differences become less important once the daily duration is included
The largest PPFD reading can provide a conservative room estimate because plants at lower-light positions receive a smaller but proportional fraction of the same DLI
rationale: DLI derived from a single bright point can overstate the daily photon dose experienced by much of the canopy. A representative spatial PPFD measurement is needed for a room-wide estimate.
